In the two decades before I became a Federal Reserve governor, I studied and contributed research to the economics of innovation and used machine learning in my research. statements.text: In general, I am optimistic about broad benefits accruing to the economy and society from the use of generative AI—including more productive and less tedious work in offices, labs, factories, and warehouses—provided we address the very real concerns I just mentioned, and others like them.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As we consider how to foster the emerging benefits of AI and guard against unwelcome harms, it is important to keep in mind that the path from innovation to greater welfare passes through the choices of individuals in a social context—in the corner office, in government, and in the minds of workers and consumers—and progress could stall or accelerate in any of these places.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Moreover, observers have noted that AI models sometimes harbor, if not amplify, the biases found in their training data, leading to malign effects on decisions about mortgage approvals, insurance rates, medical diagnoses, and even pretrial detention.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Importantly, in the policy arena—as well as health care, consumer finance, insurance, and many others—decisionmakers have legal and ethical duties to be deliberate about the effects their choices have on affected groups. In this context, an AI black box with no insight into the decision-making process is of limited value.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As a policymaker, I look upon model-generated forecasts with a skeptical eye, if they are not coupled with a plausible explanation for the driving factors behind them. More generally, when stakeholders have an opportunity to appeal a decision, they are entitled to understand how the decision was made—an issue I emphasized when I spoke at the 2018 meeting of this group.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: So I am particularly interested in seeing progress on "explainable AI," which may help bridge the divide between the technical sphere and the user.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI makes predictions, but AI does not make choices. Ultimately, human beings are still in control.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The benefit of AI to society as a whole will depend on the adaptability of workers' skills, how well they are retrained or redeployed, and how policymakers choose to support the groups that are hardest hit by these changes.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I anticipate that these advances may have a significant effect on workers, the labor market, and the economy in coming years.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The key reason why many expect AI will have a substantial effect on the economy is, because AI has the potential to provide a large and sustained boost to labor-productivity growth—which is simply how much output of an individual worker grows over time.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As a society, we will need to consider how to retrain and support workers who may be displaced from their jobs, even as many others benefit from AI adoption.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: We should expect AI to do the same: eliminating some jobs but, crucially, also creating new ones.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: It is possible that if AI adoption is rapid, we could see the effects on some workers come quickly and be more concentrated, depending on which sectors are early adopters.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: If incumbent firms are able to adjust their processes to capture productivity benefits from AI, then these firms could help mitigate some of AI's potential for job displacement by internally reallocating affected workers to new roles and providing necessary training.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: My recommendation to you is to take the time to experiment with AI, familiarizing yourself with its capabilities and limitations.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Workers in jobs that will be complemented by AI might benefit from familiarizing themselves with how to effectively use AI.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: My view is that AI, and generative AI in particular, is likely to become a general-purpose technology—one that spreads throughout the economy, sparks downstream innovation, and continues to improve over time.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: While much is still to be learned, I see growing evidence that AI is poised to have a substantial effect on U.S. and global labor markets.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Although I share the view that AI could lift productivity out of this period of low growth, it bears emphasis that recent productivity gains have been modest despite rather impressive changes in information technology.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The degree to which AI leads to productivity improvement bears careful watching, because, if it does meaningfully lift productivity, it could help constrain unit labor costs and inflation in the long run.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Moreover, a consensus needs to be forged on the benefits and costs of regulation of the use of AI in the areas of privacy, compensation for training data, perpetuation and amplification of bias, and fraud.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Some observers have noted that the finite supply of high-quality data is beginning to constrain model improvement.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Future gains are expected to be driven by the adaptation of AI to specific contexts using proprietary data available only within the confines of individual firms.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In short, AI will be translated into productivity improvements with "long and variable lags," as we monetary policymakers like to say.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI is transforming the economy, including by accelerating how quickly we generate ideas and making workers more efficient, and that, in turn, will affect both sides of our dual mandate of maximum employment and price stability.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: On the maximum-employment side of the mandate, AI can generate new tasks and jobs and possibly eliminate others, similar to many past technological innovations. On the price-stability side of our mandate, AI can improve productivity, which can lower inflationary pressures, but it can also boost prices in the interim, as AI adoption may lead to a surge in aggregate investment.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Studying the net effects of AI on the economy over time will be critical to setting appropriate monetary policy.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I want to start by stressing that any organization engaging with this technology should take a thoughtful and structured approach to AI adoption.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: First and foremost is establishing strong governance and risk management. A central tenet of good governance should be the mindset that humans are in the loop, because it ensures that people guide AI rather than allow AI to guide us.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: A second principle is that education and training of staff are critical to get and keep employees at the technological frontier. A third principle is empowerment. Teams within organizations should be encouraged to learn by doing and engage hands-on with AI technologies in controlled environments. Finally, a fourth principle is experimentation. Organizations should maintain a spirit of openness while retaining the ability to halt projects that do not meet rigorous standards.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Simultaneously, the research at the Fed is proceeding deliberately and cautiously, as many AI tools are not yet ready to be put into production.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As AI filters through the economy, it has the potential to affect both sides of our dual mandate in different ways.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I applaud SIEPR for holding this event to discuss artificial intelligence (AI) and its power to influence the trajectory of the economy and transform the financial system.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Then, consistent with my long-standing support for responsible innovation, I will address the benefits AI could deliver for the financial system before addressing some of the risks and vulnerabilities the technology presents to financial stability.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I believe AI is a technology like none other I have seen in my lifetime.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As firms incorporate AI more systematically into their production processes, I expect that AI will further boost productivity growth, contributing to my expectation that GDP will grow robustly in the near to medium term.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Policymakers and academics have noted that, increasingly, AI-driven algorithmic trading may generate financial-stability risks, such as more correlated trading, endogenous model collusion, potential market manipulation, and greater market concentration.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Recent advances in the ability of large language models (LLMs) and agentic AI systems to detect, exploit, and create new vulnerabilities have introduced new challenges in safeguarding system security for financial institutions, infrastructure, and third-party service providers.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: To be clear, as I said at the NBER Summer Institute last year, the Federal Open Market Committee is not using AI in developing or setting policy

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: With appropriate governance frameworks, autonomous intelligence can potentially expand our analytical capabilities.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I will conclude by sharing how the Fed itself is embracing the power of AI to help ensure the financial system remains sound and resilient.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Moreover, yet another shock to prices could be layered on from the heightened investment demand due to AI. To date, companies have announced more than $1.5 trillion in data-center plans, only a small portion of which have been realized.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Those figures suggest that substantial AI-related investment remains in the pipeline from data centers alone. Effects of this demand on prices are apparent. Prices have risen significantly for chips, other high-tech equipment, and software.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Furthermore, I have been and will continue to be highly attentive to AI developments and how they will affect the labor market. We could be approaching the most significant reorganization of work in generations.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Even if, in the long run, new jobs are created, I am aware that the timing of costs and benefits of AI may differ.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI is poised to become the most significant technological shift of our lifetime. I view it as a general-purpose technology, on par with or exceeding breakthroughs, such as the steam engine, electricity, and the internet. Those innovations spread throughout the economy, sparked downstream innovation, and improved over time.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: To fully recognize the benefits of AI, we must pair optimism with caution and be cognizant of valid concerns AI may pose for privacy, bias, workers, fraud, cybersecurity, and intellectual property rights.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: For our part at the Fed, as a supervisor of banking organizations, we have encouraged, and continue to encourage, responsible use of AI within the financial sector in a manner that is consistent with safe and sound practices and in compliance with applicable law.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I will continue to monitor closely the speed, direction, and magnitude of AI development as I assess the economic outlook, the appropriate path of monetary policy, and financial stability.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI affects nearly every aspect of my role at the Federal Reserve, including monetary policy, financial stability, bank supervision, financial market infrastructure, and our own operational preparedness.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In the short term, AI appears to be adding inflationary pressures to the economy, postponing inflation's return to our 2 percent target. In the medium term, while I expect that productivity growth may modestly ease those inflationary pressures, the labor market will be at risk of entering a painful transition. In the long term, I am optimistic that AI-fueled productivity growth can raise living standards for all Americans.

attribution.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.
